record.paper_title: Lower Bounds for Unrestricted Boolean Circuits: Open Problems
record.original_question: Can one prove a 5n lower bound for the Boolean-circuit size of an n-input, n-output Boolean function, that is, for some function in B_{n,n}?

evidence.quote: We use Bn,m to denote the set of all Boolean functions with n inputs and m outputs.
How to prove a 5n lower bound for a function from Bn,n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B_{n,n}$ denote the set of all Boolean functions $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^n$ with $n$ inputs and $n$ outputs. The (combinational) circuit size of $f$, denoted $C(f)$, is the minimum number of gates in a Boolean circuit over the full binary basis $B_2$ (the set of all binary Boolean operations) that computes $f$. 

Exhibit an explicit family of functions $f_n \in B_{n,n}$ together with a proof that 
$$C(f_n) \ge 5n - o(n)$$
for all sufficiently large $n$.
artifact.status_search_result: A 5n − o(n) lower bound (in fact a 7n − o(n) lower bound) for the circuit size of an explicit function in B_{n,n} has been established. Demenkov et al. and later authors give simple proofs of a 5n − o(n) lower bound for functions with few outputs and a 7n − o(n) lower bound for explicit functions with n outputs, so the question of obtaining a 5n bound for some function in B_{n,n} is solved.

status_evidence.title: New Lower Bounds on Circuit Size of Multi-output Functions
status_evidence.snippet: A 7n − o(n) lower bound for an explicit function f ∈ B_{n,n}.
status_evidence.claim: An explicit 7n − o(n) lower bound (hence > 5n) is known for some function in B_{n,n}.

status_evidence.title: An Explicit Lower Bound of 5n − o(n) for Boolean Circuits
status_evidence.snippet: Iwama–Morizumi style 5n − o(n) lower bound over U_2.
status_evidence.claim: 5n − o(n) lower bounds for explicit Boolean functions are established in the literature.
